sections.heading: Storefront Door Frame and Hardware Replacement
sections.body: Glass alone is rarely the only component that needs attention after a commercial door incident. Frames, hinges, closers, panic hardware, and locking mechanisms all experience wear over time and can be damaged in the same event that breaks the glass. Our technicians are equipped to repair or replace aluminum storefront frames, pivot systems, overhead concealed closers, floor springs, and a wide range of door hardware components. We carry commonly needed parts on our service vehicles to accelerate turnaround times for Bowie properties. Whether you manage a professional office building near the Bowie Health Campus area or a retail strip center with multiple tenant storefronts, we can coordinate repairs across multiple doors to restore a consistent, polished appearance. Getting the frame and hardware right is just as important as the glass itself — a properly aligned and secured door protects your tenants, customers, and assets around the clock.

sections.heading: Sliding, Automatic, and Specialty Commercial Door Repair
sections.body: Modern commercial properties in Bowie often feature sliding glass doors, automatic sensor-operated entrances, balanced door systems, and other specialty configurations. These systems require technicians with specific knowledge of both the mechanical and glazing components involved. Our team is experienced in repairing and replacing glass panels in sliding door tracks, recalibrating automatic door operators, and restoring balanced door pivot systems used in high-traffic lobbies and medical or institutional facilities. We also handle frameless all-glass door systems that are popular in upscale office buildings and hospitality environments. When specialty commercial doors fail, the repair requires careful attention to tolerances, alignment, and the interaction between the glass, the frame, and the operating hardware. We bring that level of detail to every job, ensuring that repaired doors operate smoothly, seal properly, and meet the functional demands of your specific building type and use.
